item.title: Cold and dry weather set for winter holiday week
item.description: Finland will see dry and cold conditions during the first winter holiday week, according to the Finnish Meteorological Institute. Forecasts issued on 12 February show daytime temperatures between -5°C and -15°C across most of the country. Night-time readings will fall further under clear skies. In southern areas, temperatures will drop to between -15°C and -20°C. In central and northern regions, lows of -20°C to -30°C are expected.

item.title: Nato approves new command unit for Finland
item.description: NATO has approved Finland’s proposal to host a Deployable CIS Module, placing a new command and control unit on Finnish soil. Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen announced the decision in Brussels on Thursday during a meeting of NATO defence ministers. “It is good news,” Häkkänen told Finnish reporters. The unit will provide communication and information system services to support NATO forces and command structures in Finland and, if required, across the alliance.

item.title: Foodora ends operations in Finland after 10 years
item.description: Foodora will cease operations in Finland at the end of February. The closure affects about 80 local employees. The company confirmed on Friday that its app and delivery service will run until 27 February 2026. After that date, the platform will shut down across the country. The decision follows change negotiations that began on 12 January. The process ended this week with a resolution to withdraw from the Finnish market.

item.title: Finland beat Sweden 4–1 in Olympic ice hockey
item.description: Finland secured a 4–1 win over Sweden in the men’s Olympic ice hockey tournament on Friday. The result delivered Finland’s first victory of the group stage after a 4–1 loss to Slovakia in the opening match. The game began at 13.10 local time and drew attention across Finland, with the long-standing rivalry adding weight to the group fixture. Goaltender Juuse Saros played a central role in the outcome.

item.title: Merz warns US against going alone at Munich summit
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the Munich Security Conference that the rules-based international order “no longer exists” and warned that the United States lacks the strength to act alone in a period of rivalry between major powers. item.title: Finland files protest over Olympic sprint waxing dispute
item.description: Finland has filed a formal protest with the International Ski Federation over events during the men’s Olympic sprint at the Milan–Cortina Winter Games, alleging rule breaches by Norway and the United States. The Finnish Ski Association and the Finnish Olympic Committee submitted the complaint to the sprint jury on Saturday morning. The protest concerns the final of Tuesday’s race, in which Norway’s Johannes Kläbo took gold ahead of American Ben Ogden and Norway’s Oskar Vike.

item.title: Finland claim relay bronze at Milan–Cortina
item.description: Finland secured bronze in the women’s 4x7.5km cross-country relay at the Milan–Cortina Winter Olympics, ending a 12-year wait for an Olympic medal in the event. The quartet of Johanna Matintalo, Kerttu Niskanen, Vilma Ryytty and Jasmi Joensuu finished third in heavy, wet snow as Norway took gold and Sweden silver. Norway won in 1:15:44.8. Sweden followed 50.9 seconds behind. Finland crossed the line 1 minute 14.7 seconds after the winners and 21.3 seconds ahead of Germany in fourth.

item.title: Five European states blame Russia for poisoning Navalny
item.description: Five European countries have concluded that Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny died after being poisoned with epibatidine, a rare toxin found in South American dart frogs, and have held the Russian state responsible. The United Kingdom, France, Germany, Sweden and the Netherlands issued a joint statement on Saturday following laboratory analysis of biological samples taken from Navalny’s body. item.title: Finland beat Italy 11-0, set Olympic ice hockey shot record
item.description: Finland beat Italy 11-0 in their final men’s Olympic ice hockey group match in Milan, registering 62 shots on goal and breaking the Olympic single-game record. The previous mark of 60 shots belonged to Sweden. Finland surpassed it in the closing minutes when Joel Kiviranta scored the team’s 11th goal. The result leaves Finland on six points and with a goal difference of +11, placing them in strong position to advance directly to the quarter-finals as the best group runner-up.
